Propensity

/pruh-PEN-sih-tee/ - the stress falls on PEN · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Propensity means a natural, built-in tendency to behave in a certain way.

Volunteers learn on day one about the raccoon's propensity to unlatch cages, and they count noses twice before locking up.

Worked Example

Bridge engineers speak of certain alloys' propensity to crack in deep cold, and they design accordingly — as though the metal will do what it is built to do, not what the brochure hopes.

A propensity is a built-in tendency: behavior that flows from how a person, animal, or material is wired, not from a passing mood. That is why the word turns up in reports and risk tables — a propensity is the pattern you predict and plan around.

How Propensity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

tendency

tendency: the neutral, all-purpose word for a recurring pattern

disposition

disposition: the overall cast of a person's nature

Antonyms

resistance

resistance: a built-in push against, rather than toward

immunity

immunity: complete protection from a pull that others feel

How Strong Is It? — leaning → propensity → obsession

leaning vs. propensity

leaning vs. propensity: A leaning is gentler than a propensity — a leaning nudges your choices, while a propensity reliably produces the same behavior again and again.

obsession vs. propensity

obsession vs. propensity: Obsession goes far beyond propensity — a propensity is a pattern others can predict, while an obsession is a pull its owner can no longer put down.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pro-

Prefix — pro-: forward

Root — pens-

Root — pens-: to hang, to weigh (Latin pendere)

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: state of

Put it together

Put it together: Pro- ('forward') + pens- (Latin pendere, 'to hang, to weigh') + -ity = the state of hanging forward. Picture a scale with one pan already tilting: a propensity is the built-in lean toward one behavior before any choosing starts. The same hanging root swings inside pendulum.

Use the root in a new word: pendulum

Use the root in a new word: pendulum: The grandfather clock's pendulum swings once a second, hanging and falling through the same arc all day.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / analytical

Propensity is the analyst's word for a wired-in behavioral pattern — the kind that appears in scouting reports, risk tables, and case files, usually trailing 'for' or 'to.' Inclination (also in this unit) is softer and more personal: a leaning you might simply indulge. Note a propensity in a report; confess an inclination over coffee.
